whole.problem: Sam drops invoice-1042.pdf in and the file is kept, but none of its words are read. A search for Total finds nothing, so Sam copies every total by hand.
whole.gets: Drop a PDF in. Get its words back, page by page, in the order a person would read them.
whole.for: Anyone at the bakery who needs to search or copy what an invoice says.
whole.in: PDFs made by software: invoices, statements, newsletters.
whole.out: Scanned pages, locked files, and tables kept as tables.
whole.assumes: You have opened a PDF. Nothing about how one is stored.
whole.unknown: Whether the fonts in real invoices carry their letter tables. Step 2 tests it.
whole.asking: Approve the five steps and answer one question, at step 5. The research found no better way than the one you asked for.

steps.text: Opener: opens the file and finds its pages
Letter reader: each shape on a page, named through its font's letter table, with where it sits
Line maker: letters into words, words into lines, lines and columns into reading order
Page by page, the words go back to Sam

step.title: Open the file and find its pages
step.label: Pages
step.caption: Invoice 1042 as Sam sees it: one page.
step.gist: A PDF keeps an index of its parts at its very end. This step reads that index and finds each page, the least that runs from one end to the other.

frames.text: The file's last lines say where the index starts: byte 48,210.
notes: A program reads a PDF from its end, because the index is written last.

frames.text: The index lists every numbered part and the byte it starts at. Beside it, `/Root` names the part everything hangs from.
notes: A file saved again adds a new index after the old one, pointing back with `/Prev`. The newest wins.

frames.text: `/Root` points to `/Pages`, a tree. Its branches list their children under `/Kids`, and its leaves are the pages.
notes: Walking the tree left to right gives the pages in order.

frames.text: Each page is handed on with its number.

how.breaks: A damaged index. The library rebuilds it by scanning the file for the start of each part, which this plan would otherwise have to write.

head: What the library also handles
How
rows: An index that is itself packed
It is unpacked like any other packed part, then read
The outer part is unpacked before the index is followed into it
Rebuilt by scanning the file for the start of each part

trade.chose: An established PDF library to open the file
trade.over: Reading the file's parts by hand
trade.because: Its index, packing and damaged-file cases are many and well handled there
trade.costs: A library for the project to keep up to date

step.title: Read every letter on a page, with where it sits
step.label: Letters
step.caption: What the file holds: shapes at places, and the font's table naming each.
step.gist: The file doesn't store words. It stores shapes and where each goes, and each font's letter table says which letter a shape is.

frames.text: A page doesn't hold text. It holds drawing steps, packed the way a zip file is (`FlateDecode`).
Unpacked, they are short commands, each written after its values.
notes: `BT` … `ET` start and end a run of text. `/F1 11 Tf` picks font F1 at 11 points.
`412 704 Td` moves to 412 across, 704 up from the bottom. `Tm` sets the place outright.
`Tj` draws shapes, given as numbers: `<112A>` is shapes 17 and 42. `TJ` also nudges them sideways.

frames.text: The font's letter table turns each number into a letter: 17 is T, 42 is o.
Each letter is kept with its place. The next one starts further right, by the shape's width times the size.
notes: A PDF measures in points, 72 to an inch, up from the bottom-left corner.
This step turns that into down from the top, so later steps read top to bottom: 704 up is 88 down here.

decides.number: A shape's width, which the font lists, times the size

how.breaks: A font with no letter table. One using a standard set of codes can still be read. One cut down to its file's shapes, numbered its own way, cannot.

list: Not known yet: how many fonts carry no letter table. This step counts them across a hundred of the bakery's invoices.

trade.chose: Naming each shape through its font's letter table
trade.over: Reading the page as a picture, letter by letter
trade.because: Software-made PDFs carry the table, and it is exact
trade.costs: A font with no letter table gives no letters at all

step.title: Put the letters into words and lines
step.label: Lines
step.caption: Invoice 1042's words, line by line.
step.gist: Letters close together make a word, and words at the same height make a line. Read top to bottom, Sam can now search for Total.

html: Total$1,284.50

frames.text: Each letter has a box: where it starts and ends across, and its baseline. The file often holds no spaces at all.
notes: The program that made the file only moved the position between words, so words and lines are worked out from the boxes.

frames.text: Sort by baseline, top to bottom. Letters whose baselines differ by less than a fifth of a letter's height are one line.
Along the line, sorted by where each letter starts, a gap wider than a third of a letter's width starts a new word.
notes: A letter here is about 5.5 wide, so the line is drawn at 1.8.

frames.text: A line's words are joined with single spaces, and the lines with line breaks.

decides.number: A fifth of a letter's height
decides.decides: Whether two letters are on one line

decides.number: A third of a letter's width
decides.decides: Whether a gap between letters is a space

how.breaks: Letters set off the baseline on purpose, such as a raised mark or a figure in another font. They can land on a line of their own.

list: Both numbers are measured against the letters themselves, so a headline and small print are each judged at their own size.

trade.chose: A gap of a third of a letter's width between words
trade.over: A fixed gap, the same for every size of letter
trade.because: Large and small type space their words differently
trade.costs: Tightly set text can run two words together

step.title: Read two columns one after the other
step.label: Columns
step.caption: The Hill Street newsletter: two stories side by side.
step.gist: Read straight across, a two-column page mixes its stories. A strip down the page with no letters in it marks the columns, and each is read whole.

notes: The file draws its text in whatever order the program that made it chose, so that order can't be trusted. The layout can.

step.title: Show the letters a font can't name
step.label: Unnamed letters
step.caption: Invoice 2207's delivery line, set in font F3.
step.gist: On 2 invoices in 100, a font has no letter table, so its letters can't be named. This step decides what Sam sees in their place.

Each shape's box is still known from step 2, so the line keeps its order, with a gap of the right width.

choices.question: When an invoice uses a font with no letter table, as 2 in 100 of the bakery's do, what should Sam see in place of those words?

today.text: Sam drops invoice-2207.pdf in and no words are read from it

choices.decides: Whether Sam needs to know a word was there and couldn't be read, or only wants the words that could.
choices.recommended: A box for each letter that can't be named, and a note naming the font
alternatives: Leave those words out, and say nothing
choices.why: A missing word Sam can see is one Sam can check on the invoice itself; one left out silently looks like a whole line.
